# API Reference

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->
<!-- Generated by crd-ref-docs (hack/crd-ref-docs) in cluster-api-provider-terraform; do not edit. Regenerate there with `make docs-gen DOCS_DIR=<this checkout>`. -->

CAPTF's CRDs are one group/version, `infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1`,
with seven kinds:

- **TerraformCluster** — the InfraCluster of Cluster API, provisioned by a Terraform/OpenTofu module.
- **TerraformClusterTemplate** — a template for TerraformClusters, used by ClusterClass.
- **TerraformMachine** — the InfraMachine of Cluster API, provisioned by a Terraform/OpenTofu module.
- **TerraformMachineTemplate** — a template for TerraformMachines, used by MachineDeployments, MachineSets, KubeadmControlPlane and ClusterClass.
- **TerraformMachinePool** — the InfraMachinePool of Cluster API, provisioned by a Terraform/OpenTofu module.
- **TerraformMachinePoolTemplate** — a template for TerraformMachinePools, used by MachinePools.
- **TerraformClusterIdentity** — cluster-scoped cloud credentials for TerraformClusters, TerraformMachines and TerraformMachinePools in allowed namespaces.

Every kind's `spec.variables` and `spec.variablesFrom`, and the module
contract they feed, are documented in [Job Inputs](../concepts/inputs.md).

## infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1

Package v1alpha1 contains the API Schema definitions for CAPTF (the
cluster-api-provider-terraform), the infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io
v1alpha1 group version. CAPTF turns a Cluster API cluster, machine or
machine pool into one Terraform or OpenTofu module run: TerraformCluster,
TerraformMachine and TerraformMachinePool carry the desired state that
CAPI's core controllers create and drive, TerraformClusterTemplate,
TerraformMachineTemplate and TerraformMachinePoolTemplate each hold a
template (their spec.template) from which a TerraformCluster,
TerraformMachine or TerraformMachinePool is created — the first typically
referenced by a ClusterClass, the second by a MachineDeployment, MachineSet
or a control-plane provider, the third by a MachinePool — and
TerraformClusterIdentity holds the cloud credentials a cluster's module run
is allowed to use, mirrored into the namespaces that reference it. Seven
kinds in all, each registered, with its List type, in
groupversion_info.go.

Every object's spec.source names the one OCI image that bundles the
module's Terraform/OpenTofu code and the runtime binary that runs it (the
image-contract types, Source and JobPolicy, live in common_types.go), and
spec.identityRef, spec.variables and spec.variablesFrom feed that module's
inputs. The controllers in internal/controllers render those inputs, run
the image as a Kubernetes Job and translate its outputs and health into the
object's status: status.conditions (see conditions_consts.go for every
condition type and reason CAPTF sets, and their Ready-summarization rules)
and the run-tracking status types common_types.go shares across the
TerraformCluster, TerraformMachine and TerraformMachinePool kinds —
ActiveJob, LastRun (with its RunStep and RunError), SourceStatus and
StateBackup — alongside the drift and remediation policy types DriftPolicy
(cluster), MachineDriftPolicy (also reused for a cluster's per-machine and
per-pool defaults), MachinePoolDriftPolicy (pool, never fully disabled) and
MachineRemediation (machine).

zz_generated.deepcopy.go is controller-gen output; regenerate it with `make
generate`, never hand-edit it. groupversion_info.go registers the group
version and every kind with the runtime scheme.

#### ApplyPolicy

_Underlying type:_ _string_

ApplyPolicy decides whether a TerraformCluster applies a change on its
own or waits until its plan is approved.

_Validation:_

- Enum: [Automatic Manual]

_Appears in:_

- [TerraformClusterSpec](#terraformclusterspec)

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Automatic` | ApplyPolicyAutomatic applies every change as soon as it is seen, only<br />guarded against destructive plans.<br /> |
| `Manual` | ApplyPolicyManual plans every change first (a plan Job), shows the<br />plan in status.plan and applies it only once ApprovePlanAnnotation<br />names its hash. The first apply of a new cluster is not gated.<br /> |

#### JobPolicy

JobPolicy tunes the Kubernetes Jobs that run the module. Every field is
optional. On a TerraformMachine or TerraformMachinePool the policy is
merged field by field with TerraformCluster.spec.defaults.jobs: a field
the machine or pool sets wins, an unset one comes from the defaults, and
a field neither sets gets the controller's built-in default. env is
merged by name (the machine's or pool's wins on the same name) and
imagePullSecrets is the union (the machine's or pool's first); resources,
securityContext and podSecurityContext are replaced as a whole. Defaults
are resolved at reconcile time and never persisted, so a provider upgrade
reaches existing objects. Jobs never retry pods (backoffLimit 0) and never
get a TTL: the controller owns retries and prunes finished Jobs itself.

_Appears in:_

- [TerraformClusterDefaults](#terraformclusterdefaults)
- [TerraformClusterSpec](#terraformclusterspec)
- [TerraformMachinePoolSpec](#terraformmachinepoolspec)
- [TerraformMachineSpec](#terraformmachinespec)
- [WorkspaceSpec](#workspacespec)

| Field | Description | Required | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `successfulJobsHistoryLimit` _integer_ | successfulJobsHistoryLimit is how many succeeded Jobs to keep per object<br />and operation. The newest succeeded Job of each operation is kept even<br />at 0. Defaults to 3, applied at reconcile. | No | | Maximum: 100 <br /> Minimum: 0 <br /> |
| `failedJobsHistoryLimit` _integer_ | failedJobsHistoryLimit is how many failed Jobs to keep per object and<br />operation. The newest failed Job of an operation is kept even at 0<br />while no newer Job of that operation succeeded: retry backoff counts<br />it. Defaults to 3, applied at reconcile. | No | | Maximum: 100 <br /> Minimum: 0 <br /> |
| `activeDeadlineSeconds` _integer_ | activeDeadlineSeconds bounds a Job's run time, in seconds, at most one<br />day. Defaults to 3600, applied at reconcile when unset (0). When a<br />policy sets both, lockTimeoutSeconds must be less than<br />activeDeadlineSeconds. | No | | Maximum: 86400 <br /> Minimum: 1 <br /> |
| `serviceAccountName` _string_ | serviceAccountName overrides the runner ServiceAccount. When unset the<br />controller creates captf-runner, bound to the static captf-runner<br />ClusterRole. An override ServiceAccount must exist and carry the label<br />captf.io/runner=true, or no Job is created. | No | | MaxLength: 253 <br /> MinLength: 1 <br /> |
| `lockTimeoutSeconds` _integer_ | lockTimeoutSeconds is passed to the runtime as -lock-timeout, in seconds.<br />Defaults to 300, applied at reconcile. | No | | Maximum: 3600 <br /> Minimum: 0 <br /> |
| `imagePullSecrets` _[LocalObjectReference](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.36/#localobjectreference-v1-core) array_ | imagePullSecrets for the Job pod: they cover the source image and the<br />runner init image. | No | | MaxItems: 10 <br /> MinItems: 1 <br /> |
| `resources` _[ResourceRequirements](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.36/#resourcerequirements-v1-core)_ | resources of the main container. | No | | |
| `env` _[EnvVar](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.36/#envvar-v1-core) array_ | env adds environment variables to the main container. It cannot override<br />the TF_\* and KUBE_\* variables the runner sets. | No | | MaxItems: 64 <br /> MinItems: 1 <br /> |
| `securityContext` _[SecurityContext](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.36/#securitycontext-v1-core)_ | securityContext of the main container. Defaults, applied when the Job is<br />built: seccompProfile RuntimeDefault, capabilities drop ALL,<br />allowPrivilegeEscalation false, readOnlyRootFilesystem true. runAsNonRoot<br />is not defaulted. The webhook rejects privileged: true,<br />allowPrivilegeEscalation: true and any capabilities.add: the container<br />holds cloud credentials. | No | | |
| `podSecurityContext` _[PodSecurityContext](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.36/#podsecuritycontext-v1-core)_ | podSecurityContext of the Job pod. Defaults, applied when the Job is<br />built: seccompProfile RuntimeDefault. | No | | |

#### MachineDriftPolicy

MachineDriftPolicy configures periodic drift detection of a
TerraformMachine. Drift on a machine is always reported, never remediated:
the machine is immutable infrastructure, replaced by a rollout.

_Appears in:_

- [TerraformClusterDefaults](#terraformclusterdefaults)
- [TerraformMachineSpec](#terraformmachinespec)

| Field | Description | Required | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `intervalSeconds` _integer_ | intervalSeconds between drift checks, in seconds. Defaults to the<br />manager's --drift-default-interval (30m), applied at reconcile. 0<br />disables drift checks. Unless remediation.annotateMachine is true<br />(which refreshes at remediation.healthCheckIntervalSeconds), that also<br />stops every health sample after provisioning. | No | | Minimum: 0 <br /> |

#### MachinePoolDriftPolicy

MachinePoolDriftPolicy configures periodic drift detection of a
TerraformMachinePool. Unlike MachineDriftPolicy, 0 is rejected by the CRD
schema: for a pool it is membership refresh
(TerraformMachinePoolSpec.MembershipRefreshIntervalSeconds), not drift,
that keeps status fresh (https://captf.io/docs/module-author/contract/v1alpha1/machinepool.html
"Membership refresh"), and the drift Job itself feeds the refreshed
replicas into its plan (machinepool.md "Drift order"), so disabling
drift would also stop that refresh from ever reaching a plan.

_Appears in:_

- [TerraformMachinePoolSpec](#terraformmachinepoolspec)

| Field | Description | Required | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `intervalSeconds` _integer_ | intervalSeconds between drift checks, in seconds. Defaults to the<br />manager's --drift-default-interval (30m), applied at reconcile when<br />unset (0). Unlike a machine's or the cluster's, a pool's drift cannot<br />be disabled, so 0 always means "use the default", never "disabled". | No | | Minimum: 1 <br /> |
| `action` _[DriftAction](#driftaction)_ | action taken when drift is found: Report or Remediate. Defaults to<br />Report, applied at reconcile. Unlike a machine's, a pool's drift may<br />be remediated: the group's instances are not immutable infrastructure. | No | | Enum: [Report Remediate] <br /> |

#### MachineRemediation

MachineRemediation configures how a TerraformMachine signals an unhealthy
instance to Cluster API beyond its Ready condition.

_Appears in:_

- [TerraformMachineSpec](#terraformmachinespec)

| Field | Description | Required | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `annotateMachine` _boolean_ | annotateMachine sets cluster.x-k8s.io/remediate-machine on the owner<br />Machine once the instance has been unhealthy for unhealthyThreshold<br />consecutive samples, or at once when it is terminated. CAPTF removes<br />the annotation it set once the instance reads Healthy again and the<br />Machine is not being deleted; an annotation set by anyone else is left<br />alone. It has an effect only when a MachineHealthCheck selects the<br />Machine; a single-replica control plane refuses the remediation.<br />Defaults to false. | No | | |
| `unhealthyThreshold` _integer_ | unhealthyThreshold is the number of consecutive unhealthy health samples<br />before the Machine is annotated. A sample is one completed refresh or<br />drift Job. Defaults to 3, applied at reconcile when unset (0). A<br />terminated instance counts on the first sample. | No | | Maximum: 100 <br /> Minimum: 1 <br /> |
| `healthCheckIntervalSeconds` _integer_ | healthCheckIntervalSeconds is how often a provisioned machine is<br />refreshed to sample its health while annotateMachine is true,<br />independent of drift.intervalSeconds. Defaults to 300, applied at<br />reconcile when unset (0). With annotateMachine false it is ignored and<br />health is re-read only at the drift (or refresh) cadence, so<br />drift.intervalSeconds 0 then stops health sampling after provisioning. | No | | Maximum: 86400 <br /> Minimum: 60 <br /> |

#### Operation

_Underlying type:_ _string_

Operation is one of the operations a Job runs.

_Validation:_

- Enum: [apply destroy drift refresh restore plan]

_Appears in:_

- [ActiveJob](#activejob)
- [LastRun](#lastrun)

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `apply` | OperationApply creates or updates the infrastructure.<br /> |
| `destroy` | OperationDestroy destroys the infrastructure.<br /> |
| `drift` | OperationDrift refreshes state and plans to detect drift.<br /> |
| `refresh` | OperationRefresh refreshes state and outputs only.<br /> |
| `restore` | OperationRestore pushes a state backup back into the backend<br />(RestoreStateAnnotation).<br /> |
| `plan` | OperationPlan plans a TerraformCluster's change for review and<br />applies nothing (applyPolicy Manual).<br /> |

#### RunErrorKind

_Underlying type:_ _string_

RunErrorKind classifies a failed run.

_Validation:_

- Enum: [image-layout step interrupted blocked plan-changed]

_Appears in:_

- [RunError](#runerror)

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `image-layout` | RunErrorKindImageLayout means the image does not follow the image contract.<br /> |
| `step` | RunErrorKindStep means a runtime step failed.<br /> |
| `interrupted` | RunErrorKindInterrupted means the step was stopped from outside (the<br />pod got SIGTERM: a drain, an eviction, a Job deletion or its deadline),<br />not that the module failed.<br /> |
| `blocked` | RunErrorKindBlocked means a TerraformCluster apply stopped before a<br />plan that deletes or replaces resources, because the<br />captf.io/approve-destructive-plan annotation does not name the<br />inputs hash it renders. Nothing was changed.<br /> |
| `plan-changed` | RunErrorKindPlanChanged means a TerraformCluster apply approved for<br />one plan (applyPolicy Manual, captf.io/approve-plan) planned other<br />changes and stopped before applying them. Nothing was changed; the<br />new plan waits for its own approval in status.plan.<br /> |

#### Source

Source is the deliverable: one OCI image that bundles the role module's
Terraform/OpenTofu code and the runtime binary. There is no separate module
source and no separate runtime image. The image layout is a fixed-path
contract: /captf/module, /captf/runtime and an optional /captf/providers
mirror. The runner always execs /captf/runtime;
pull secrets for the image are jobs.imagePullSecrets.

_Appears in:_

- [TerraformClusterSpec](#terraformclusterspec)
- [TerraformMachinePoolSpec](#terraformmachinepoolspec)
- [TerraformMachineSpec](#terraformmachinespec)
- [WorkspaceSpec](#workspacespec)

| Field | Description | Required | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image` _string_ | image is the OCI image reference, registry/repo:tag or<br />registry/repo@sha256:digest. The tag or digest is the module version.<br />Referencing an image grants its publisher Secret-read and cloud-credential<br />access in this namespace. | Yes | | MaxLength: 512 <br /> MinLength: 1 <br /> |
| `imagePullPolicy` _[PullPolicy](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.36/#pullpolicy-v1-core)_ | imagePullPolicy for the image. Defaults to IfNotPresent, applied when the<br />Job is built; Always is recommended for mutable tags. | No | | Enum: [IfNotPresent Always Never] <br /> |

durable inputs Secret or the Job list, because clusterctl move does not
restore status.

_Validation:_

- MinProperties: 1

- [TerraformCluster](#terraformcluster)

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `initialization` _[Initialization](#initialization)_ | initialization is the v1beta2 contract's initialization status. | No | | MinProperties: 1 <br /> |
| `observedGeneration` _integer_ | observedGeneration is the generation this status was computed for. | No | | Minimum: 1 <br /> |
| `activeJob` _[ActiveJob](#activejob)_ | activeJob is the Job currently running for this object, if any. | No | | |
| `lastRun` _[LastRun](#lastrun)_ | lastRun is the result of the most recent completed Job. | No | | |
| `lastDriftCheck` _[Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.36/#time-v1-meta)_ | lastDriftCheck is when the last drift check completed. | No | | |
| `lastRefresh` _[Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.36/#time-v1-meta)_ | lastRefresh is when the last refresh or drift check completed, or,<br />for a kind whose apply itself can give a definite health reading,<br />when that apply finished instead (that reading stands in for the<br />refresh after the apply). | No | | |
| `pendingRefreshes` _integer_ | pendingRefreshes counts the consecutive health samples (completed<br />refresh or drift Jobs) that read pending since the last other reading<br />or the last apply; unset otherwise. It spaces the refreshes while<br />health is pending: 30s, then 1m, 2m, 4m and at most 5m. It lives in<br />status only, so it restarts at 0 (30s) after clusterctl move. | No | | Minimum: 1 <br /> |
| `observedStateSerial` _integer_ | observedStateSerial is the Terraform state serial the outputs were read<br />from. | No | | Minimum: 1 <br /> |
| `stateSecretSuffix` _string_ | stateSecretSuffix is the kubernetes backend secret_suffix of this<br />object's state. Informational: the controller derives it<br />deterministically. | No | | MaxLength: 63 <br /> MinLength: 1 <br /> |
| `source` _[SourceStatus](#sourcestatus)_ | source records what the last Job actually ran. | No | | MinProperties: 1 <br /> |
| `stateBackups` _[StateBackup](#statebackup) array_ | stateBackups are the state backups the controller keeps (newest<br />first), as of the last backup, prune or restore request. | No | | MaxItems: 16 <br /> MinItems: 1 <br /> |
| `failureDomains` _[FailureDomain](https://pkg.go.dev/sigs.k8s.io/cluster-api/api@v1.14.2/core/v1beta2#FailureDomain) array_ | failureDomains reported by the module's failure_domains output. | No | | MaxItems: 100 <br /> MinItems: 1 <br /> |
| `plan` _[PlanPreview](#planpreview)_ | plan is the plan of the change waiting for approval under<br />applyPolicy Manual; empty when none waits. Approve it by setting the<br />captf.io/approve-plan annotation to plan.planHash. | No | | |

#### TerraformMachineSpec

TerraformMachineSpec is the desired state of a TerraformMachine: the
machine-role module image and how to run it. source, identityRef,
variables and variablesFrom define the machine and are immutable after
creation, and providerID can only be
set once, by the controller; the admission webhook enforces this. jobs,
drift and remediation are operational policy and may change at any time.

_Validation:_

- MinProperties: 1

_Appears in:_

- [TerraformMachine](#terraformmachine)
- [TerraformMachineTemplateResource](#terraformmachinetemplateresource)

| Field | Description | Required | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `providerID` _string_ | providerID is the instance's provider ID, set by the controller from the<br />module's provider_id output. It must equal the Node's spec.providerID. | No | | MaxLength: 512 <br /> MinLength: 1 <br /> |
| `source` _[Source](#source)_ | source is the role image: module code and runtime. | Yes | | |
| `identityRef` _[IdentityReference](#identityreference)_ | identityRef names the TerraformClusterIdentity whose credentials this<br />object's Jobs use. Whether it is required, and where it falls back to<br />when unset, depends on the kind. | No | | |
| `jobs` _[JobPolicy](#jobpolicy)_ | jobs tunes the Jobs that run this object's module. On a kind that<br />inherits defaults it is merged field by field over them (see<br />JobPolicy). | No | | |
| `variables` _[RawExtension](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.36/#rawextension-runtime-pkg)_ | variables are module variables, a JSON object: each key becomes a<br />named argument of the role module, converted by the module's declared<br />type. Keys are Terraform identifiers; captf_ names and the role's<br />contract inputs are reserved. Inline variables win over variablesFrom.<br />Whether a change re-applies or is rejected as immutable depends on the<br />kind. A key the module does not declare fails the apply ("Unsupported<br />argument"). | No | | MaxProperties: 256 <br /> MinProperties: 1 <br /> Type: object <br /> |
| `variablesFrom` _[VariablesSource](#variablessource) array_ | variablesFrom reads module variables from ConfigMaps and Secrets in<br />this namespace labeled captf.io/variables=true, in list order: a later<br />source wins on the same key, and inline variables win over all of<br />them. Whether and when a change to a referenced source takes effect<br />depends on the kind. | No | | ExactlyOneOf: [configMapRef secretRef] <br /> MaxItems: 16 <br /> MinItems: 1 <br /> |
| `drift` _[MachineDriftPolicy](#machinedriftpolicy)_ | drift is merged field by field over the cluster's defaults.drift. Drift<br />on a machine is always reported, never remediated. | No | | |
| `remediation` _[MachineRemediation](#machineremediation)_ | remediation configures how an unhealthy instance is signalled to<br />Cluster API beyond the Ready condition. | No | | |

#### VariablesFormat

_Underlying type:_ _string_

VariablesFormat is how the data values of a variablesFrom source are
passed to the module.

_Validation:_

- Enum: [String JSON]

_Appears in:_

- [VariablesSource](#variablessource)

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `String` | VariablesFormatString passes each data value as a string. The module's<br />declared variable type converts it ("3" to a number, "true" to a bool).<br /> |
| `JSON` | VariablesFormatJSON parses each data value as JSON, for lists, maps<br />and objects. A value that is not valid JSON is VariablesInvalid.<br /> |

#### VariablesSource

VariablesSource reads module variables from the data of one ConfigMap or
Secret in the object's namespace: every data key becomes a variable of the
same name. The source must carry the label captf.io/variables=true.
Variables from a Secret are declared sensitive in the generated root, so
Terraform redacts them in plan and apply output; they are still stored in
the inputs Secrets and in state, like every input.

_Validation:_

- ExactlyOneOf: [configMapRef secretRef]

_Appears in:_

- [TerraformClusterSpec](#terraformclusterspec)
- [TerraformMachinePoolSpec](#terraformmachinepoolspec)
- [TerraformMachineSpec](#terraformmachinespec)
- [WorkspaceSpec](#workspacespec)

| Field | Description | Required | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `configMapRef` _[VariablesSourceReference](#variablessourcereference)_ | configMapRef names a ConfigMap. Exactly one of configMapRef and<br />secretRef is set. | No | | |
| `secretRef` _[VariablesSourceReference](#variablessourcereference)_ | secretRef names a Secret. Exactly one of configMapRef and secretRef is<br />set. | No | | |
| `optional` _boolean_ | optional makes a missing or unlabeled source contribute nothing<br />instead of holding the object at DependenciesReady False<br />(VariablesSourceNotFound). Defaults to false. | No | | |
| `format` _[VariablesFormat](#variablesformat)_ | format of the data values: String passes each value as a string, JSON<br />parses each as JSON. Defaults to String, applied at reconcile. | No | | Enum: [String JSON] <br /> |

#### VariablesSourceReference

VariablesSourceReference names a ConfigMap or Secret in the object's own
namespace.

_Appears in:_

- [VariablesSource](#variablessource)

| Field | Description | Required | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` _string_ | name of the ConfigMap or Secret. | Yes | | MaxLength: 253 <br /> MinLength: 1 <br /> Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*$` <br /> |
